_doc: Per-domain routing for URL handling. Two consumer surfaces today: (1) /wiki-capture cascade (head_preserving / auth_required / default) via extract_page_metadata.py; (2) /wiki-corroborate credibility classification (credibility_tier_1/2/3 / credibility_denylist) via extract_page_metadata.classify_credibility(). Lists grow at user-decision gates via confirmed proposals — never silently. Three pattern shapes supported: 'host' (exact + subdomain match — e.g., 'medium.com' matches medium.com and any *.medium.com); '*.tld' (wildcard suffix — e.g., '*.edu' matches cs.berkeley.edu); 'host/path' (path-prefix — e.g., 'linkedin.com/in/' matches linkedin.com/in/karpathy but not linkedin.com/posts/...). Tier checks run in priority order tier_1 → tier_2 → tier_3 → denylist, so path-prefix vendor entries (e.g., 'github.com/anthropic') in tier_1 take precedence over a bare 'github.com' fallback in tier_3.
_head_preserving_doc: Domains where urllib is blocked (4xx / timeout / Cloudflare) but WebFetch's preprocessor preserves <head> metadata. Path 1 fires (WebFetch with extended metadata prompt). Add ONLY after user-confirmed verification that the WebFetch metadata is real and not hallucinated (round-2 probe finding, 2026-05-08). May stay empty in practice — most reachable cases are covered by Path 3 (urllib). Reference case: arxiv.org passes through head, but urllib also reaches arxiv.org so it stays as default.
_auth_required_doc: Domains known to require an authenticated browser session (Cloudflare bot-fight, paywalls, login walls). /wiki-capture skips fetch entirely and redirects the user to the Obsidian Web Clipper (or Chrome capture / paste). Seed: medium.com (verified 2026-05-08 — returns 403 even with Mozilla User-Agent in stdlib urllib).
_credibility_tier_1_doc: Primary / authoritative sources. Vendor official docs, peer-reviewed papers, standards bodies, .edu/.gov, official vendor GitHub + HuggingFace orgs (path-prefix match), peer-reviewed conference proceedings (PMLR / NeurIPS / ACL / IEEE Xplore). Seed list extends on user confirmation at /wiki-corroborate decision gate when an unclassified domain returns a high-quality hit. github.com/<vendor> and huggingface.co/<vendor> are kept symmetric — model weights distribution carries the same authority as code distribution. Bare github.com / huggingface.co (in tier-3) is the fallback for unaffiliated user repos / community blog posts.
_credibility_tier_2_doc: Established secondary sources with editorial standards. Named publications, established trade press, known-authority personal sites, LinkedIn profile pages (in/ path-prefix only — distinct from posts/pulse). Seed list extends on user confirmation.
_credibility_tier_3_doc: Community / personal blogs. Useful but not authoritative. Bare github.com / gist.github.com here is the fallback for non-vendor repos (tier-1 path-prefix vendor entries match first). The --include-tier-3 flag on /wiki-corroborate surfaces these alongside tier-1+tier-2; the default cut excludes them.
_credibility_denylist_doc: Default-skip — content farms, anonymous threads, marketing posts. linkedin.com/posts/ + linkedin.com/pulse/ path-prefixes are denylisted while linkedin.com/in/ stays in tier-2 (profile pages are bio-evidence; LinkedIn marketing posts aren't).
